title: The screen in the truck
summary: The screen in the R.E.P.O. truck is a machine of its own: the menu has antennas, panels, windows and a dish on springs, and the display reveals text, shows chat messages and changes its background.
body: The screen in the truck is not a flat panel. The menu around it is animated: antennas, a front panel, two windows and a dish each have a spring with a target of their own, so the whole console moves as the truck does.
Every part of the console has two ends. The middle antenna, the front panel, both windows, the dish and the back antenna each keep a transform and a target, which is where the spring pulls them to.

It has debris of its own. There are particles for skeleton bits and smoke at the start and again at the end, along with a loop and sounds for swerving, speeding up and slowing down, which is how the truck console reacts to being driven.

The text is held as an object of its own. It carries a static grab collider, the message string it is showing, a callback for when a chat message arrives, an engine success sound and a test line kept for building, which is why what you read on the screen is driven rather than printed.
The display has settings for how text arrives. There is a reveal setting and a delay between one message and the next, so the text can be typed out rather than appearing all at once.

Messages are their own object. There is a screen type, a chat message with a loading bar and a result bar with a light of its own, so a message can be shown while it is being worked on and then resolved.

It has sounds for its own typing. There are separate sounds for typing, for emoji, for a new line, for a new page and a loop while a message is charging, along with custom emoji sounds, which is why the console can sound busy without anything being said.
A message can succeed or fail, and the screen has four background colours: its main one, an off one, an evil one and one used while it is changing.

Engine sounds belong to the screen as well. There is a transform for the engine sound, a rev sound and a success sound, which is how the audio of the truck is attached to what is on the display rather than to the vehicle alone.
Because the menu, the text and the sounds are all part of one object, the truck can be torn apart and put back together without the console losing what it was showing.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the colour texture of the screen in the truck.
What this entry does not tell you: what any message says, how long a message takes, or what the success and failure states change. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The truck menu is animated, with antennas, a front panel, two windows and a dish each on a spring with a target.
facts.evidence: identifiers: TruckMenuAnimated, antennaMiddleSpring, frontPanelSpring, windowLeftSpring, windowRightSpring, dishSpring, antennaBackSpring

facts.claim: Each of those parts also keeps a transform and a target of its own.
facts.evidence: identifiers: antennaMiddleTransform, antennaMiddleTarget, frontPanelTransform, frontPanelTarget, windowRightTransform, windowRightTarget, windowLeftTransform, windowLeftTarget, dishTransform, dishTarget, antennaBackTransform, antennaBackTarget

facts.claim: It has skeleton bit and smoke particles at the start and at the end, plus a loop and swerve, speed-up and slow-down sounds.
facts.evidence: identifiers: particleSkeletonBitsFirst, particleSkeletonSmokeFirst, particleSkeletonBitsLast, particleSkeletonSmokeLast, soundLoop, soundSwerve, soundSpeedUp, soundSlowDown

facts.claim: The display has a text reveal setting and a delay between messages.
A message has a screen type, a loading bar and a result bar with a light of its own.
facts.evidence: identifiers: screenType, chatMessage, chatMessageLoadingBar, chatMessageResultBar, chatMessageResultBarLight

facts.claim: It has typing, emoji, new line, new page and charge loop sounds, with custom emoji sounds of its own.
facts.evidence: identifiers: typingSound, emojiSound, newLineSound, newPageSound, chargeChatLoop, customEmojiSounds

facts.claim: A message can succeed or fail, and the screen has main, off, evil and transition background colours.
facts.evidence: identifiers: chatMessageResultSuccess, chatMessageResultFail, mainBackgroundColor, offBackgroundColor, evilBackgroundColor, transitionBackgroundColor

facts.claim: Engine sounds are attached to the screen as well.
The screen opens on a curve, and its door has a loop that is started and ended separately.
facts.evidence: identifiers: TruckScreenOpen, openScreenCurve, doorLoop, doorLoopStart, doorLoopEnd

facts.claim: The truck's body rustles in three long and three short sounds, its skeleton hits have sounds of their own including the skull, and there are faster swerves and fire-pass swerves.
facts.evidence: identifiers: soundBodyRustleLong01, soundBodyRustleLong02, soundBodyRustleLong03, soundBodyRustleShort01, soundBodyRustleShort02, soundBodyRustleShort03, soundSkeletonHit, soundSkeletonHitSkull, soundSwerveFast01, soundSwerveFast02, soundFirePass, soundFirePassSwerve01, soundFirePassSwerve02

facts.claim: The screen's text carries a static grab collider, the chat message it shows, a callback for when a message arrives, an engine success sound of its own and a test line kept for building.
facts.evidence: identifiers: TruckScreenText, staticGrabCollider, chatMessageString, onChatMessage, engineSuccessSound, testingText

facts.claim: The screen itself has both a colour texture and a normal map of its own.
facts.evidence: asset names: Truck Screen_DefaultMaterial_BaseColor, Truck Screen_DefaultMaterial_Normal

alt.zh: 示意图：卡车控制台随弹簧晃动，信息逐字打出并有专属音效，随后以成功或失败收尾。

sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each fact is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
